interactions.summary: Jiang asks the class why surrender would be the correct choice even under full faith in God, then extends the thought experiment by asking what the friend would do once Piccarda gives in.
A student says surrender becomes morally different once the mother's life is also at stake, because the choice no longer concerns Piccarda alone.
A student reasons that the friend would likely recoil from the marriage because the alliance now looks morally tainted and politically self-defeating rather than useful.
Jiang steers the class from sympathy toward political motive, pressing them to name that the marriage was always about alliance and power rather than romance or piety.

claims.claim: Jiang says that even if Piccarda has complete faith in God, surrender is still the correct choice once refusing would expose her mother to execution.
A student argues that the moral calculus changes because the threat now implicates another life, so the choice is no longer a matter of Piccarda sacrificing only herself.
Jiang treats the friend's perspective as politically instrumental: the marriage matters because it secures alliance and power, not because of personal affection.
The student concludes that the friend could plausibly withdraw because the coercive marriage would cost him power, public legitimacy, and the very alliance he wanted to secure.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang bluntly states that complete faith in God still points toward surrender in this case.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the correct choice would be to surrender
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's hardest reversal, because faith does not produce heroic defiance here but submission for the sake of another life.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang reduces the marriage to naked alliance logic and makes the class say out loud that the desired end was power.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps Dante's moral problem tied to political ambition rather than letting it drift into abstract theology.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The real political purpose of the proposed marriage, which lets Jiang reinterpret the vow as a power bargain rather than a romantic or sacramental act.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-18 Jiang ties Piccarda's surrender directly to collateral responsibility and then pivots immediately into the political logic of alliance, showing that faith and power are being tested in the same scenario.
